A personal brand spread across a website, a report, and a talk usually means three themes drifting apart.

`mcanouil` is one extension carrying all three: a project type for the website, and formats for HTML, Typst, and RevealJS that share a `brand.yml`, a component set, and a look.

[See a report rendered by this site](preview.pdf).

![](preview.pdf){.embed-art loading="lazy" title="A report rendered by mcanouil-typst"}

## Installation

```bash
quarto add {{< var extension.reference >}}
```

This will install the extension under the `_extensions` subdirectory.
If you are using version control, you will want to check in this directory.

::: {.btn-group role="group" aria-label="Quarto Wizard installer options"}

[Visual Studio Code](vscode://mcanouil.quarto-wizard/install?repo={{< var extension.wizard-reference >}}){.btn .btn-outline-primary title="Install {{< var extension.reference >}} in Visual Studio Code using the Quarto Wizard extension."}

## Quick start

A website:

```yaml
project:
  type: mcanouil
```

A document, a report, or a deck:

```yaml
format: mcanouil-html
```

```yaml
format:
  mcanouil-typst:
    style: professional
    brand-mode: light
```

```yaml
format:
  mcanouil-revealjs:
    brand-mode: dark
```

See the [Reference](reference.qmd) for the three formats and what they share, and the [Examples](examples.qmd) for worked front matter.

## Where it works

HTML, Typst, and RevealJS, plus the project type that ties a website together.
